title: ARM Q-Channel device-side controller: qreqn / qacceptn / qdeny / qactive handshake (RUN, REQUEST, STOPPED, EXIT, DENIED), activity from software events, illegal controller sequences flagged

fields.desc: write 1: an activity event; qactive stays high for ACT_CYCLES (16) clocks after the last one, and a request while it is high is denied

regs.name: STATUS
regs.desc: Q-Channel outputs, as driven on the pins

fields.desc: low: the device accepted the request and is stopped (STOPPED and EXIT)
high: the request was denied (DENIED, until qreqn rises)
high: activity within the last ACT_CYCLES clocks

irqs.name: ILLEGAL
irqs.desc: the controller broke the handshake: qreqn rose before the device answered a request, or fell during the exit

irqs.name: DENIED
irqs.desc: a request was denied; set on every clock qdeny is high, so a clear only holds once qreqn has risen

notes: qreqn is the controller's request pin; it passes through unchanged and is sampled on PCLK. qacceptn, qdeny and qactive drive the Q-Channel pins and are also readable in STATUS.

A request (qreqn low) is decided in the clock after it is seen: accepted (qacceptn low) when the device is idle, denied (qdeny high) when qactive is high. Only software activity events (EVENT) make the device active.
